findings.comment: Ground-to-sky clearances within electric easements are not maintained or shown. The site plan and grading plan show buildings and site improvements near easement boundaries, but do not dimension vertical clearances or confirm that structures do not encroach from ground to sky within the easement area. Please show (via dimension line or note) that all buildings, structures, utilities, and permanent site improvements maintain ground-to-sky clearance (no vertical encroachment) from easement boundaries, or clarify exactly how close structures approach the easement in both horizontal and vertical directions.
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas and all structures within 15 feet of easement boundaries
findings.observation: Examined the site plan (Sheet 9) and grading plan (Sheet 11) for any ground-to-sky clearance dimensions or notes. Vision analysis of Sheet 11 confirmed: 'There are **no** ground-to-sky clearances, structural setback dimensions from buildings to easements, or related clearance notes visible on this sheet.' The site plan shows buildings and site improvements near easement boundaries, but provides NO clearance dimensions from building edges, roof lines, canopies, awnings, structures, or landscaping to the easement boundaries. The grading plan similarly shows no special treatment or clearance zones within easement areas. While the electrical design plan notes that all electric infrastructure is underground (which eliminates the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement for overhead conductors), UCM § 1.10.10.2 prohibits ground-to-sky encroachment within electric and telecommunications easements for ANY type of structure, site amenity, or permanent improvement.
findings.reasoning: Although all electric facilities shown on this project are underground distribution, UCM § 1.10.10.2 still prohibits permanent structures, buildings, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other improvements from encroaching from ground to sky within electric easements. The requirement protects Austin Energy's right to access, maintain, and potentially upgrade easement areas. The site plan must explicitly show or dimension how much clearance (if any) exists between building footprints, hardscape, and other improvements and the recorded easement boundaries. Without ground-to-sky clearance dimensions or a note confirming that structures do not extend into the easement area (vertically), compliance cannot be verified. The vision analysis confirmed such dimensions are absent from the plans.

findings.comment: Ground-to-sky clearances within electric easements are not maintained; existing trees, retaining walls, fencing, and other permanent site improvements are shown directly overlapping easement boundaries. Remove all trees within electric easement boundaries or shown within 15 feet of overhead conductors. Relocate concrete retaining walls and pond perimeter fencing outside easement boundaries or provide written approval from Austin Energy for placement within easements. Provide tree removal and landscape modification details demonstrating 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radius clearance from overhead conductors per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Electric easement areas on east, south, and northeast portions of property; areas with overhead electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts numerous existing trees (shown as scalloped and dashed circles) overlapping electric easement boundaries. Vision analysis confirms: 'Numerous existing tree symbols (scalloped and dashed circles) are mapped directly overlapping the eastern Greenbelt Access & Use Easement, 15' Easement, and 5' Electric Easement...Tree symbols also heavily overlap the 25' Drainage Easement in the NE corner and the 5' Elec. Easement on the south perimeter.' Additionally, the vision analysis identifies: 'A heavy Concrete Retaining Wall runs continuously inside the North, East, and South perimeters, acting as a physical barrier... A Wood Fence is labeled running along the far East property line...A Pond Perimeter Fence circles the NE corner pond.' Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) notes transformer pads are 'located in spaces...suggesting these facilities sit in unpaved, landscaped, or natural surface areas.' The site plan shows the retaining wall running through/along the boundary of the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement, and a detention pond with associated fencing directly occupies the 25' Drainage Easement area. No clearance dimensions or tree removal callouts are shown demonstrating that ground-to-sky clearance is maintained.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors within electric easements, and a 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Trees within electric easements create permanent obstructions that violate these clearances and restrict Austin Energy's ability to access and maintain overhead and underground facilities. The presence of trees shown directly overlapping easements, combined with the absence of any tree removal or clearing callouts, demonstrates non-compliance. Further, the concrete retaining wall and associated fence structures running through easement boundaries create physical obstructions that prevent equipment access and violate the ground-to-sky clearance requirement. The grouping's common violation pattern explicitly lists this deficiency: 'Site plan shows building overhang, awning, canopy, or permanent structure extending into or over electric easement, violating ground-to-sky clearance requirement.' Here, trees, walls, and fencing occupy that space.

findings.comment: Ground-to-sky clearances within electric easements and electric and telecommunications easements (ETE) not maintained; buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, trees, overhead features, or other improvements encroach from ground to sky. Existing trees overlap or are immediately adjacent to overhead electric lines along the southern property boundary, violating the minimum 15-foot lateral clearance required from overhead conductors. Provide a tree preservation and removal plan that either demonstrates 15-foot minimum clearance from overhead conductors will be maintained or identifies trees for removal/pruning to comply with clearance requirements.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric (OHE) lines and existing trees are located
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Electrical Design Plan (Sheet 21) explicitly states: 'Existing tree symbols (large circles) do overlap the existing OHE (overhead electric) lines running along the southern boundary.' Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) confirms existing trees are shown adjacent to the OHE lines along the southern property line. The Grading Plan (Sheet 11) shows contour lines and existing tree symbols in the area of the OHE lines. The General Notes (Sheet 3) require that 'Austin Energy has the right to prune and/or remove trees...to keep the easements clear' and state that 'Trees: Minimum 15 lateral feet from overhead conductors or equipment' (from the regulatory overview). The current condition shows existing trees overlapping or immediately adjacent to overhead electric lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 specifies 'Permanent Clearances From AE Overhead Distribution Lines and Facilities: 7.5 feet minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead conductors' and '15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors.' UCM § 1.10.10.2 addresses ground-to-sky clearances and customer activities in easements. The regulatory overview explicitly requires 'Trees: Minimum 15 lateral feet from overhead conductors or equipment.' The vision analysis documenting tree symbols overlapping OHE lines indicates that existing ground cover and trees are encroaching into the 15-foot clearance zone required by code. The site plan must demonstrate that existing trees and vegetation do not violate the 15-foot clearance requirement or be removed/pruned to comply.

findings.comment: Public Utility Easements are not clearly kept free of buildings, structures, and other improvements. The site plan shows site improvements near PUE boundaries, but provides no notation confirming that any improvements within or adjacent to PUEs have received written approval from Austin Energy per UCM § 1.5.2.1.L. Please either: (1) relocate all improvements outside PUE boundaries, or (2) provide documentation of written Austin Energy approval for any improvements within PUE boundaries and add a note to the site plan confirming this approval.
applicableAreas: All Public Utility Easements on site
findings.observation: Examined the site plan (Sheet 9) and grading plan (Sheet 11) for improvements within or near Public Utility Easement boundaries. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows recorded PUE boundaries (e.g., '5' P.U.E.' and '7.5' P.U.E.') depicted as dashed lines. The site plan shows driveways, parking areas, and other site improvements in proximity to PUE boundaries. However, the plans do NOT include any notation indicating that improvements within or adjacent to PUEs have received written approval from Austin Energy per UCM § 1.5.2.1.L. The general notes on Sheet 3 include: 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date' but include NO reference to Austin Energy written approval requirements for improvements within existing PUEs.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and § 1.5.2.1.L establish that customer facilities (buildings, structures, site amenities, utilities, landscaping) shall NOT be installed within PUEs without written approval from Austin Energy. The grouping guidance identifies 'Improvements in PUE without approval' as a common violation pattern. The applicant must demonstrate that any improvements shown within or adjacent to PUE boundaries have received Austin Energy written approval. The absence of such notation on the plans means either: (1) the applicant intends to place improvements within the PUE without approval (a deficiency), or (2) approval exists but was not documented on the plans (also a deficiency). The plans must include a note confirming Austin Energy has reviewed and approved any proposed improvements within PUE boundaries.

findings.comment: Public Utility Easements are not kept clear of site improvements; detention pond with retaining walls and fencing are shown directly within the 25' Drainage Easement in the NE corner. Additionally, critical recorded easements (Greenbelt Access & Use Easement and City of Austin Drainage Easement per facts.md) are not depicted on site plan despite being perpetual encumbrances. Revise site plan to: (1) Depict and label all recorded easements including Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137); (2) Remove detention pond, retaining walls, and fencing from within easement boundaries or provide written approval from Austin Energy and City of Austin Watershed Protection; (3) Relocate Building 4 or other structures outside easement buffers; (4) Provide notation on all sheets that improvements have received written AE/City approval if any structures remain within easements.
applicableAreas: Public Utility Easements on north, east, and northeast property; specifically 25' Drainage Easement area and Greenbelt Access & Use Easement
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows Building 4 positioned 27.3' from the east property line, placing it immediately adjacent to the Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (which occupies NE interior per facts.md). The site plan shows a continuous Concrete Retaining Wall running along the eastern boundary directly adjacent to/through the Greenbelt easement boundary. Vision analysis confirms: 'An Infiltration/Detention Pond and Concrete Retaining Wall sit directly inside the 25' Drainage Easement in the northeast corner...A Concrete Retaining Wall encircles it and Pond Perimeter Fence.' The detention pond structure, retaining walls, and pond fencing represent permanent site improvements placed directly within the 25' Drainage Easement area. Facts.md documents that two critical easements are NOT depicted on the submitted site plan: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (0.31 acres, NE interior—a perpetual no-build zone per recorded Instrument 2010070731); and (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (0.130 acres, NE corner—per recorded Instrument 2011021137). Despite being recorded and binding on the property, these easements were not shown on site plan submittal, yet building placement and pond placement proceed as if these easements do not constrain the layout.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and UCM § 1.5.2.1.L require that Public Utility Easements serving electric facilities be kept clear of buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other permanent improvements without written approval from Austin Energy. The site plan affirmatively shows permanent structures (detention pond with retaining walls and fencing) placed within the 25' Drainage Easement area in the NE corner. These improvements have not been annotated with notation of AE written approval. The Greenbelt easement situation is even more problematic: it is a perpetual no-build zone per the recorded instrument, yet it was not depicted on the site plan, indicating the applicant either did not account for it in the design or deliberately omitted it. Facts.md explicitly states these easements 'must be depicted before approval' and that 'proposed building layout must be evaluated against both easement footprints.' The combined two easements encumber approximately 0.44 acres (~19% of the 2.16-acre site), yet neither is shown on the submitted plans. This constitutes a fundamental deficiency in PUE documentation and compliance.

findings.comment: Public Utility Easements (PUE) not kept clear of buildings, structures, utilities, site amenities, landscaping, and other improvements. The site plan does not clearly specify which improvements (if any) will be placed within PUE boundaries, nor does it document written Austin Energy approval for any such improvements. Clarify which site amenities, landscaping, and other improvements will be located within PUE boundaries. If any improvements are proposed within PUEs, provide notation on the plans indicating written Austin Energy approval for those specific improvements.
applicableAreas: Public Utility Easements containing or adjacent to electric facilities (north, east, and southeast property boundaries)
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows PUEs along property boundaries and existing trees/landscaping nearby. The Landscape Plan (Sheet 31) shows landscaping features throughout the site. However, the site plan does not provide a detailed specification of which site amenities and landscaping will be placed within PUE boundaries versus outside them. The plans do not include notation of 'written Austin Energy approval' for any improvements within or near PUEs. The general notes do not address specific approvals for landscaping or other site improvements within PUEs. Without detailed improvements plan notes on the PUE areas, it is unclear whether final landscaping and site amenities will encroach into PUE boundaries without required written approval from Austin Energy.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.5.2.1.L requires that 'Customer facilities in easements require AE written approval.' UCM § 1.10.10.2 addresses customer activities in utility easements. The site plan must either show that no improvements are planned within PUE boundaries, or provide notation of written AE approval for any landscaping, trees, or other site amenities to be located within PUE areas. The lack of detailed specification about which improvements (if any) will be within PUEs creates ambiguity about compliance.

findings.comment: Unable to verify whether proposed trees block access to or overhang electric vaults due to lack of vault/manhole coordination on Landscape Plan.
applicableAreas: Electric vaults
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows pull boxes and transformers. Sheet 31 does not show pull boxes, vaults, or manhole locations. If subsurface electric equipment exists, its locations not depicted on Landscape Plan.
findings.reasoning: Cannot verify tree canopy clearance from vault lids without vault locations shown on Landscape Plan.

findings.comment: Show vault locations on the landscape plan with tree locations and estimated mature canopy spreads. Verify no trees are positioned to create overhead obstruction of vault covers/lids.
applicableAreas: Electric vault locations throughout site
findings.observation: Vault locations shown on Sheet 21 are not shown on landscape plan (Sheet 31). Vault covers/lids must remain clear of tree canopy for operational access, but without vault locations on the landscape plan, this cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires that vaults remain accessible for personnel and equipment. Trees positioned over vault covers prevent access operations. The landscape plan must show vault locations and tree canopy spreads to verify compliance.

findings.comment: Concrete retaining walls, Type III driveway, and concrete sidewalk are shown encroaching into the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Relocate all structures and permanent improvements outside the electric easement boundaries, or provide evidence that these easements have been abandoned or modified. Coordinate with Austin Energy to verify easement status.
applicableAreas: southern 5' electric easement boundary
eastern 5' electric easement boundary
southern and eastern property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depict 5' electric easements along the southern boundary ('5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.Tx.') and eastern boundary ('5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.'). On Sheet 9, multiple improvements are drawn directly overlapping or encroaching into these easement boundaries: (1) A Type III Driveway with notation 'Construct Type III Driveway See Detail 1/335-2' crosses completely through the southern 5' electric easement; (2) A 6' Concrete Sidewalk labeled 'Construct 6' Concrete Sidewalk See Dtl 4/335-1' crosses through the southern 5' easement; (3) Concrete Retaining Wall lines with notation 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall at Existing Concrete Retaining Wall Tie to Existing Concrete Retaining Wall' overlap and encroach into both the southern and eastern 5' easement areas, running parallel to the easement boundaries. These structures are drawn directly on or overlapping the dashed easement boundary lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly prohibits permanent structures, buildings, overhangs, balconies, canopies, stairways, eaves, awnings, patios, roofed structures, and permanent improvements (including below-grade footings) within electric easements. Driveways, sidewalks, and retaining walls are permanent improvements. The site plan clearly depicts these improvements overlapping the drawn easement boundary lines. The graphic evidence from Sheet 9 shows these structures encroaching into the dedicated easement areas. UCM § 1.10.10.2 is absolute: 'no structures are permitted above or below grade' within electric easements; the site plan violates this prohibition.

findings.comment: Concrete retaining wall enclosing the detention pond is located within the 5' Electric Easement and must be removed or relocated outside the easement. No permanent structures are permitted within electric easements where Austin Energy must maintain 24-hour access to facilities.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identified the concrete retaining wall enclosing the biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeastern corner. The vision tool analysis explicitly states: 'Yes, the Biofiltration/Detention Pond overlaps. The eastern edge of the "Concrete Retaining Wall" enclosing the pond is drawn completely within the 5-foot space between the dashed easement line and the eastern property line.' This retaining wall is a permanent improvement structure (not an electric facility) within the 5' electric easement boundary. The plat (Sheet 2) labels 5' electric easements along property boundaries. The site plan shows the retaining wall within this 5-foot zone.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and the grouping description state: 'No permanent structures, buildings, swimming pools, or improvements (including below-grade footings) are allowed within electric easements.' A concrete retaining wall is explicitly a permanent improvement. The vision analysis confirmed it is within the 5' electric easement. The fundamental prohibition applies: no permanent structures above or below grade in electric easements are permitted.

findings.comment: A permanent wood privacy fence is shown within the eastern 5' electric easement. Remove the fence from the easement, or if a removable wooden fence is intended, provide documentation of a license agreement from Austin Energy and specifications clearly identifying the fence as removable to permit Austin Energy maintenance access.
applicableAreas: eastern 5' electric easement area near southeast portion of site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts a line labeled 'Wood Fence' running along the property boundary directly within the eastern 5' Electric Easement area (Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.). The site plan detail references and notes indicate this is a wooden privacy fence as part of the landscaping/site amenity design ('wooden privacy fence' notations visible in landscape and site plan details). A wooden privacy fence is a permanent structure designed to remain in place; it is not removable. The fence is located between Building 6 and the eastern property boundary, directly overlapping the dashed easement line.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 contains an exception: 'Removable wooden fences may be allowed in easements under license agreement if removable to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access.' However, the prohibition is clear for permanent or masonry fencing. The site plan shows a 'privacy fence,' which by nature and nomenclature is a permanent landscape feature not designed for removal. There is no notation stating the fence is removable or that a license agreement allows its installation. The fence is depicted as a permanent improvement within the easement area, directly violating UCM § 1.10.10.2.

findings.comment: If wooden privacy fence is located within the 5' Electric Easement, provide detail sheet specifications confirming it is removable and readily can be removed to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. Alternatively, provide executed license agreement from Austin Energy authorizing the fence installation. Permanent fencing is not permitted in electric easements.
applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) identified: 'Wooden Privacy Fence: A line with 'x' marks runs along the eastern boundary, which corresponds to Key Note "H-6" ("WOODEN PRIVACY FENCE").' The fence is shown running along the eastern property boundary where the 5' Electric Easement is located. The landscape plan does not indicate whether this fence is removable or permanent construction. Standard wood privacy fences are typically permanent installations anchored with set footings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 allows: 'Removable wooden fences may be allowed in easements under license agreement if removable to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access.' However, non-removable or permanent fencing prevents access. The landscape plan shows a wooden privacy fence along the eastern boundary within the electric easement area but provides no specification indicating it is removable or that a license agreement exists. The deficiency is unclear because the fence material (wood) suggests it might be removable, but the details do not confirm this, and no license agreement documentation is provided.

findings.comment: Electrical vaults, pedestals, and pull boxes are located throughout the site, but 8-foot clearances are not documented with dimensions or callouts. Provide plan views with dimensions and professional engineer certification verifying that a minimum 8-foot clearance in all directions is maintained around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, and electrical equipment requiring personnel access.
applicableAreas: electrical vault easement area west of Building 8
multiple electrical pull box locations throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies a 'Vault Easement' on the west side of Building 8, with an adjacent 'Electrical Pull Box.' Multiple 'Electrical Pull Box' locations are marked throughout the site (north of Bldg. 1, north of Bldg. 3, northeast of Bldg. 4, west of Bldg. 2, central corridor, east of Bldg. 6, and others). However, no dimensions, clearance measurements, or distance callouts on Sheet 21 verify that structures, landscaping, or improvements maintain the required minimum 8-foot clearance around these pedestals, subsurface vaults, or equipment access points in all directions. The electrical plan shows building footprints, driveways, and other site features in proximity to these equipment locations but provides no specific distance verification or engineer notation confirming 8-foot clearances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires 'minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access.' This is a quantified, measurable requirement. The site plan identifies multiple electrical vaults and pull boxes but provides no measurements or callouts demonstrating that the required 8-foot clearance is maintained around these facilities in all directions. While the clearance may in fact be maintained, the applicant has not provided documentation or certification of this compliance. The burden is on the applicant to affirmatively demonstrate that the requirement is met; the absence of this documentation prevents verification.

findings.comment: Provide utility coordination documentation from Austin Energy identifying all subsurface vaults, pedestals, and maintenance access points. Ensure all structures and improvements maintain 8-foot minimum clearance from these access points in all directions.
applicableAreas: Pedestals, vaults, and manhole locations throughout site
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identified four electrical transformer pad locations. These are pad-mounted (surface) units, not subsurface vaults. The plans do not show any underground pedestals, subsurface vaults, or Austin Energy maintenance access points (separate from building-owned transformers). The presence of subsurface Austin Energy electric vaults or pedestals requiring 8-foot personnel access clearance is not indicated on the electrical plans provided.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.25 requires: '8 feet of clearance from pedestals, subsurface Austin Energy vaults, or manholes that require personnel access.' The application shows distribution transformers but does not explicitly show or identify Austin Energy-owned subsurface vaults or pedestals separate from the building service infrastructure. If such Austin Energy infrastructure exists underground, the plans do not depict it. Marked 'unclear' because the actual presence of Austin Energy vaults/pedestals requiring this clearance is not confirmed on available plans.

findings.comment: Show vault and manhole locations from Sheet 21 on the landscape plan. Mark 8-foot clearance zones around each vault/manhole requiring personnel access and verify shrubs and obstructions are outside these zones.
applicableAreas: Subsurface electric vaults and manhole locations
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows vault and manhole locations (including a labeled 'Vault Easement' at transformer pad near Bldg. 8). Sheet 31 does not show these vault/manhole locations. Without them overlaid on the landscape plan, the required 8-foot clearance zone around vaults/manholes cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access. The landscape plan must show vault/manhole locations to enable verification.

findings.comment: Provide dimensioned parking layout plan explicitly showing that all parking areas and paved surfaces are located outside the 5' Electric Easement boundaries. Confirm parking is setback minimum distance from easement lines.
applicableAreas: Areas within 5' Electric Easement
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows the site layout with buildings positioned primarily on the western and central portions. The 5' Electric Easements are located along the eastern and southern property boundaries. The parking areas and driveways appear to be located in the central and western areas, separated from the easement boundaries by the building clusters. However, no explicit dimension callouts confirm the exact distance of parking areas from the easement lines. The southern parking area location relative to the southern electric easement boundary is not dimensioned.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.17 prohibits: 'Parking lots, parking areas, covered parking structures, or paved surfaces within electric distribution easements (voltage below 60kV, not transmission).' While visual inspection suggests parking is positioned away from the easements, specific dimension callouts confirming minimum clearances are absent. Marked 'unclear' because the evidence is not definitive enough to confirm the parking is entirely outside the distribution easement boundaries.

findings.comment: Permanent wood fencing is shown within 5-foot electric easements on eastern and southern property boundaries. UCM § 1.10.10.2 permits only removable wooden fences under license agreement. Either: (1) remove fencing from easement boundaries and relocate outside easement areas, (2) replace with removable fence type with notation indicating removable design allowing Austin Energy access, or (3) obtain executed license agreement from Austin Energy permitting the fence type proposed. Provide details showing fence construction and removability certification if fences will remain within easements.
applicableAreas: Wood fencing along eastern and southern property boundaries within 5-foot electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows fencing lines drawn directly along the eastern and southern property boundaries. These same property boundaries have 5-foot electric easements dedicated to utility use (labeled on Sheet 9 as '5' Electric Easement Vol. 60...' on the east and '5' Elec. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 885...' on the south). The fence lines follow the property boundary, placing them within the 5-foot easement width. The site plan notes describe these as 'Wood Fence' (eastern boundary), consistent with a typical residential privacy fence constructed of wood. Site plan details and notes do not identify these fences as removable, temporary, or specially designed to allow Austin Energy access. Standard residential wood fencing would constitute a permanent, non-removable obstruction within the easement.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly allows removable wooden fences within electric easements under a license agreement if they permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. However, it prohibits permanent or non-removable fencing. The distinction is critical: 'removable wooden fences' implies temporary structures that can be taken down during maintenance, whereas standard residential wood fences (which appear to be shown on Sheet 9) are permanent structures. The submitted plans do not specify that these fences are removable or designed for Austin Energy access. Additionally, there is no documented license agreement for easement use (per EL-5.11), which would be a prerequisite even for removable fencing. The presence of permanent-appearing wood fences within the easements violates the prohibition on non-removable fencing.
